page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processors running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 96293.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 85426.66, which ranks in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads reaching 7649.82 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server processes LLM inference prompts at 10308.98 tokens/second and generates text at 377.14 tokens/second using a 135M model. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top tier at 615.79 GB/sec.

A key architectural tradeoff is the absence of local storage, as the instance lists no bundled local disks, requiring external storage attachments. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated instances. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU and system memory resources makes this server a specialized platform for heavy parallel processing, balancing high-tier compute capabilities against shared CPU allocation.

This server configuration is designed for workloads requiring massive parallel computation and large memory footprints. Appropriate use cases include large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, complex physics simulations, and high-throughput database operations.
